implementation_notes: In JavaScript the mock is a function: jest.fn() returns a callable whose .mock.calls/.mock.results record every invocation, mockReturnValueOnce/mockImplementation programme answers, jest.spyOn(object, 'method') replaces a single method on a real object, and expect(fn).toHaveBeenCalledWith(...)/toHaveBeenCalledTimes(n) perform the verification, while jest.mock('module') substitutes a whole module. The classic mock class disappears because objects are structural and functions are first-class; a hand-written recording function is only justified when the test must run without a runner-provided mock library.
pitfalls: jest.mock factories are hoisted above imports and cannot reference module-scope variables unless they are declared through jest.hoisted or mock-prefixed names, which produces surprising ReferenceErrors.
Mocks and modules are not reset automatically; without clearMocks/restoreMocks configuration, recorded calls from one test leak into the next.
Auto-mocking a module yields functions that return undefined, so a test can pass while exercising no meaningful answer path.
